title: 2155. All Divisions With the Highest Score of a Binary Array

examples.explanation: Division at index - 0: numsleft is []. numsright is [0,0,1,0]. The score is 0 + 1 = 1. - 1: numsleft is [0]. numsright is [0,1,0]. The score is 1 + 1 = 2. - 2: numsleft is [0,0]. numsright is [1,0]. The score is 2 + 1 = 3. - 3: numsleft is [0,0,1]. numsright is [0]. The score is 2 + 0 = 2. - 4: numsleft is [0,0,1,0]. numsright is []. The score is 3 + 0 = 3. Indices 2 and 4 both have the highest possible division score 3. Note the answer [4,2] would also be accepted.

Division at index - 0: numsleft is []. numsright is [0,0,0]. The score is 0 + 0 = 0. - 1: numsleft is [0]. numsright is [0,0]. The score is 1 + 0 = 1. - 2: numsleft is [0,0]. numsright is [0]. The score is 2 + 0 = 2. - 3: numsleft is [0,0,0]. numsright is []. The score is 3 + 0 = 3. Only index 3 has the highest possible division score 3.

Division at index - 0: numsleft is []. numsright is [1,1]. The score is 0 + 2 = 2. - 1: numsleft is [1]. numsright is [1]. The score is 0 + 1 = 1. - 2: numsleft is [1,1]. numsright is []. The score is 0 + 0 = 0. Only index 0 has the highest possible division score 2.

hints: When you iterate the array, maintain the number of zeros and ones on the left side. Can you quickly calculate the number of ones on the right side?
The number of ones on the right side equals the number of ones in the whole array minus the number of ones on the left side.
Alternatively, you can quickly calculate it by using a prefix sum array.
